record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Construct the ultraviolet limit of the two-dimensional O(N) nonlinear sigma model, viewed here as an asymptotically free bosonic field theory.

evidence.quote: Construct the ultraviolet limit of the two dimensional O(N) non linear sigma model, which is a well behaved asymptotically free bosonic field theory

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional O(N) nonlinear sigma model with N ≥ 3. Its formal Euclidean action is
S(φ) = (1/2g) ∫_{R^2} |∇φ(x)|^2 dx,
where the field φ : R^2 → S^{N-1} takes values in the unit sphere in R^N and g > 0 is a coupling constant. A natural ultraviolet regularization is obtained by replacing R^2 with the lattice εZ^2 (lattice spacing ε > 0) and taking the Gibbs probability measure
dμ_{ε,g(ε)}(φ) ∝ exp( - (1/(2g(ε))) Σ_{x ∼ y} |φ(x) − φ(y)|^2 ) Π_x dσ(φ(x)),
where dσ is the uniform measure on S^{N-1} and the sum runs over nearest-neighbor pairs. Because the model is perturbatively asymptotically free, one expects that there is a choice of bare coupling g(ε) → 0 as ε → 0 (running according to the two-dimensional renormalization group with non-trivial beta function) such that the rescaled measures μ_{ε,g(ε)} converge to a non-trivial continuum probability measure on (a suitable space of) S^{N-1}-valued tempered distributions on R^2, whose correlation functions satisfy the Osterwalder–Schrader axioms and exhibit a mass gap.

Problem: rigorously construct this ultraviolet (continuum) limit. That is, exhibit a choice of bare coupling g(ε) and prove the existence of a non-Gaussian Euclidean quantum field theory on R^2 arising as the limit ε → 0 of the above lattice measures, verifying the standard Osterwalder–Schrader (or Wightman) axioms, asymptotic freedom of the renormalization-group flow, and dynamical mass generation.
artifact.status_search_result: The rigorous construction of the ultraviolet (continuum) limit of the two-dimensional O(N) nonlinear sigma model is widely regarded as an open problem in constructive quantum field theory. Despite extensive perturbative and lattice work, and recent progress on related questions (e.g., mass generation in the large-N linear sigma model, gradient-flow renormalization), no full constructive proof of the continuum limit verifying Osterwalder–Schrader axioms, asymptotic freedom, and a mass gap has been established.

status_evidence.title: Mass generation for the two dimensional O(N) Linear Sigma Model in the large N limit
status_evidence.snippet: The continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(N) linear sigma model has never been constructed, despite much progress...
status_evidence.claim: Construction of the continuum limit of the 2D O(N) sigma model remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Renormalizability of the gradient flow in the 2D O(N) non-linear sigma model
status_evidence.snippet: The gradient flow in the 2D O(N) non-linear sigma model possesses UV finiteness properties without multiplicative wave function renormalization.
status_evidence.claim: Related perturbative renormalization results exist, but do not constitute a constructive UV limit.
